battle.name: 東硤石谷之戰
battle.brief: 唐聖功二年（697），東突厥默啜部南侵河套，唐遣薛仁貴與契苾明率禁軍邊軍出塞追擊，於陰山北麓東硤谷擊潰突厥騎兵，斬首千餘級、俘人畜十餘萬。卡面所配科林斯青銅盔並非此役實有之物，卻是冷兵器騎戰中以整片金屬兜鍪換取頭顱防護的典型象徵。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 東突厥汗國與唐朝在漠南正面交鋒。突厥一方以默啜可汗為首，帳下牙帳騎兵居中樞，屬部控弦之士分屯各部帳，徵發丁壯、驅畜隨軍，來去以弓馬為長；唐一方則以北衙禁軍為骨幹，雜以朔州、五原、靈州諸軍與幽州兵，另徵鐵勒契苾部等內附部眾為嚮導。史載此役屬追擊戰，唐軍自雲中、五原一帶出塞，尋得突厥部眾於東硤谷而逼之入谷，部署一為追、一為遁，故雙方兵力的配置都以速進與散騎脫離為要。唐軍的後勤仍靠邊鎮屯田所出芻粟與內地運來的布帛器械，遠征一旦深入草原，糧秣能否接濟便是最吃緊的一環；突厥則自備馬奶酒、酪乾與帳帳，邊走邊牧，雖無後勤線，卻也不虞斷糧。關於出戰兵員的具體編制，兩《唐書》與《資治通鑑》都未細載，諸說並存。僅可知唐軍的進擊方向是由雲中、五原指向陰山以北的牧地，而突厥的撤退方向與部眾的散聚方式，史料俱未明言。
countriesEn: The Eastern Turkic Khaganate and the Tang court met face to face south of the Gobi desert. On the Turkic side the enthroned Khagan, Muqie, held the centre of the host with his own tent guard, while the string-bowmen of the various tribal camps were posted separately, with conscripted able-bodied men and their herds driven along with the column; speed of horse and bow was their strength. The Tang force was built around the Northern Palace guards, mixed with the armies of Shuozhou, Wuyuan and Lingzhou and with troops drawn from Youzhou, and it took with it Tiele tribesmen such as the Qiebi under Tang allegiance to serve as guides. The sources treat this as a pursuit: the Tang army marched out from the frontier districts around Yunzhong and Wuyuan, caught the Turkic masses at Dongxie Valley and forced them into the defile, so that the deployments of both sides turned on quick advance for one and scattered flight for the other. Tang logistics still depended on fodder and grain from the frontier garrisons and on cloth and equipment carried from the interior, and once a column drove deep into the steppe the question of keeping it supplied became the most pressing concern. The Turks by contrast carried their own mare's milk, dried cheese and tentage with them and grazed as they marched; with no line of supply to break, they were never in that difficulty. The exact establishment of the Tang army is not itemised in the Old and New Tang histories or in the Comprehensive Mirror, and the accounts differ on the point. All that can be said is that the Tang thrust ran from Yunzhong and Wuyuan towards the pastures north of Yinshan, while the direction in which the Turks withdrew and the way their people and herds were scattered are nowhere stated.
people: 此役在史籍中提及最多的是薛仁貴（名禮，字仁貴，絳州龍門人）。他自募兵起家，征高句麗、平吐蕃皆有軍功，晚年以行軍總管出塞，與契苾明等追突厥於東硤谷。契苾明是鐵勒契苾部首領，內附唐朝後受封燕然郡王，熟悉漠南部落的地形、習俗與騎射戰法，是唐軍在草原上最難得的嚮導；他既通曉突厥的用兵習慣，也清楚部帳分布與水源所在，遇到追擊便能指出該往哪一道山谷收網。突厥之主默啜可汗此時已整合汗國，控弦之士北盡漠南，屢次南下與唐相持；史載其部眾於東硤谷為唐軍所敗。此外，參戰各部首領與將官的姓名多被略去，史家往往只以「薛仁貴等」一句概括帶過。各書對將領名位、參戰部隊與出戰經過的記載詳略不一，諸說並存，難以一一核實。薛仁貴的部曲多來自河東，契苾明所部則為漠北熟習騎射之眾，兩種人馬在行軍節奏與作戰習慣上未必相同，史料對此亦無記載。
peopleEn: The figure most often named in the sources for this campaign is Xue Rengui, whose personal name was Li and whose courtesy name was Rengui, a native of Longmen in Jiangzhou. He began as a self-recruited soldier, earned distinction in the wars against Goguryeo and against the Tibetans, and in his later years marched out of the passes as commander of the column, pursuing the Turks to Dongxie Valley together with Qieming and others. Qieming was a chief of the Tiele Qiebi tribe who had come over to Tang and was granted the title of Prince of Yanran; he knew the terrain, the customs and the mounted archery of the steppe peoples better than anyone, and was the most valuable guide the Tang army had in the grassland. He understood the Turkic way of fighting, and he knew where the tribal camps stood and where water could be found, so that in a pursuit he could point out the valley into which the fugitives should be driven. The ruler of the Turks, the Khagan Muqie, had by then welded the khaganate together, and his bowmen ranged across the southern steppe, raiding south and holding the Tang at bay; the records state that his forces were defeated by the Tang at Dongxie Valley. The names of the tribal chiefs and officers who took part are mostly passed over, the annalists frequently compressing the command into a single phrase about Xue Rengui and the rest. The books differ in detail over the ranks of the commanders, the composition of the army and the course of the fighting, so several points remain uncertain and irreconcilable. Xue Rengui's soldiers were for the most part drawn from Hedong, while Qieming's men were steppe riders used to the saddle; that two such different contingents moved at a different pace and fought by different habits is a point on which the histories are silent.
kits: 卡面所列的科林斯青銅盔製作於前七世紀的希臘，與本役並無直接關係，只能作為冷兵器時代金屬頭盔的原型來看：全開式面甲加護鼻，正面遮蔽整個頭面，視野極窄，戴著者只能靠隊形與相互掩護活命。唐軍實際的防護是明光鎧配兜鍪，外罩札甲；騎兵用長刀、橫刀與槊，步兵執長槊列拒馬，弓弩備箭數百；攻城與野戰另有發石車、彈車、天兵、雲梯諸器。突厥騎兵多披獸皮或革甲，髡髮結辮，主用角弓與骨鏃箭，佩短矛、套索與環首刀，並攜馬奶酒、酪乾以供長途奔襲。兩軍都把馬視為戰力的根本，唐軍重甲騎兵數量有限，卻能以長槊與弓弩掩護散騎游騎，這正是打谷地戰的長處；而盔甲的取捨、視野的開闔，最後也就決定了山谷裏誰能先看清對方、誰能先把箭放出去。此外，草原上的刀、矛、弓之外，尚有飲水、皮革與繩索之屬，看似雜物，實則決定遠征隊伍能走多遠。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card face was made in Greece in the seventh century BC and has no direct connection with this campaign; it can only be read as a type-piece for the metal head armour of the pre-gunpowder age. Its fully enclosed visor with a nasal bar covers the whole front of the head and leaves a very narrow field of view, so that a wearer survives only by discipline and by mutual cover. The real protection of the Tang troops was a bright cuirass with a helmet over it, covered by lamellar armour; cavalry carried long sabres, straight swords and lances, infantry held long lances in a bristling line, and bows and crossbows were supplied with several hundred arrows each. Siege and field artillery included stone-throwing carts, spring-carts, battering beams and scaling ladders. Turkic riders generally wore beast hides or leather armour, their hair shaven and braided, and they relied on horn bows with bone-tipped arrows, short spears, lassos and ring-pommel sabres, carrying mare's milk and dried cheese for long rides. Both sides treated the horse as the root of military power; the Tang had few fully armoured riders, yet they could screen loose mounted skirmishers with the lance and the bow, and that was exactly their strength in a valley fight. The choice of head armour, and the opening or closing of the sight line, decided in the end who in the valley saw the enemy first and who loosed the first arrows. Beyond the blades, lances and bows, the grassland also required water skins, hide and cordage, which look like incidental gear but in truth decide how far a marching column can get.
tactics: 這是一場典型的漠北追擊戰。唐軍先以輕騎散哨探路，斷突厥水源與牧地，再以步兵長槊陣與騎兵交替掩護，把敵人從可汲水處趕入狹窄谷道；待突厥人馬擁塞難以展開，前隊以弓弩覆射，兩翼騎隊繞出截斷歸路，待其行列散亂才以長槊陣正面壓上。追擊中還常以牲畜群先行，驅群向敵陣方向以為疑兵，掩護騎兵逼近。突厥方面的求生之道是散騎脫離、揚塵遮蔽，趁唐軍分兵與糧秣不接時重整行列。谷地地形放大了唐軍步騎混編的優勢，也令潰兵無處迴旋；唐軍同樣受制於谷道狹長，追擊至後段時往往只能分割殲之。及至殘部退上谷側高地，又須仰攻方能收功，故一場勝仗往往打上數日，糧秣先竭而兵疲繼之。追擊之難，正在於敵可逸而我難返，縱然一時斬獲極豐，返程所需芻粟仍須另行籌畫。
tacticsEn: This was a textbook pursuit fight on the steppe. The Tang first sent light horse in loose pickets to scout and to cut the Turks off from water and pasture, then used infantry lances and cavalry in turn to cover one another, driving the enemy away from the places where water could be drawn and into a narrow defile. Once the Turkic horsemen were massed and unable to deploy, the vanguard covered them with arrows while mounted wings rode around to cut the line of retreat, and only when their order had broken did the lance wall press in from the front. Another device of the pursuit was to put herds of cattle in front, driving them towards the enemy as a feint while mounted troops closed in behind the confusion. The Turkic answer was to break away in scattered groups, raise dust to hide the movement and reform while the Tang were divided and short of supplies. The valley enlarged the advantage of the Tang mix of foot and horse, and it left the routed with nowhere to turn; the Tang too were cramped by the long narrow floor of the gorge, and in the later stages of the chase they could only cut the fleeing enemy into separate groups and destroy them piecemeal. When the remnants finally took to the heights along the valley side, the Tang had to assault uphill before the work could be finished, so a single victory often consumed several days, with supplies running out and the troops tiring in turn. The difficulty of pursuit lies in the fact that the enemy can slip away while the pursuer cannot turn back, so however rich the spoil of the moment, the fodder needed for the return journey still had to be reckoned separately.
data: 關於此役的數字，多出自兩《唐書》與《資治通鑑》一類史籍的簡略記載，諸說並存：一般記唐軍斬首千餘級，俘獲突厥人畜十餘萬，並以所得馬牛充軍實；出戰兵力、追擊里程與雙方損失則多闕而不詳。依行程推知，遠征須自雲中、五原一帶出塞，行程以數百里計，糧秣須備數旬，芻粟多賴邊鎮屯田與沿途收穫。作戰季節多繫於秋末冬初，草原已寒，人畜皆須就地取給，然確月則無從考定。史官於「斬首千餘級」之外並無更細的編制記載；所謂「人畜十餘萬」之中亦含牛羊駱駝，不宜逕作人數去解。故此役雖有斬獲可數，仍不宜在此補上任何具體的師兵力數或傷亡數字。所得人畜既眾，遣送、羈管與編入屯田安置的開支亦不在小數，而史籍恰恰未留下任何一筆帳目。
dataEn: The figures for this campaign come mostly from brief notices in the Old and New Tang histories and in the Comprehensive Mirror, and the accounts do not agree. The usual statement is that the Tang army cut off more than a thousand heads and captured Turkic people and livestock numbering in excess of one hundred thousand, with the horses and cattle taken serving as booty; the numbers engaged, the length of the pursuit and the losses on both sides are largely unrecorded. Judging by the distances involved, the expedition must have marched out from the Yunzhong and Wuyuan frontier districts, covered several hundred li, and had to carry fodder and grain for a number of tens of days, drawing largely on the frontier garrisons and on what could be gathered along the route. The season is generally assigned to the end of autumn or the beginning of winter, when the steppe is already cold and both men and animals must live off the land, though the exact month cannot be established. Beyond the phrase about a thousand heads taken, the annalists left no finer establishment returns; the figure of a hundred thousand people and livestock also embraces cattle, sheep and camels, and should not simply be read as a head count of persons. The victory therefore has figures that can be cited, but no specific order of battle and no casualty return should be supplied here. With so many people and animals taken, the cost of escorting, quartering and settling them on the farms was no small matter either, and the histories happen to leave not one item of account.
cause: 直接起因是東突厥的南進壓力。默啜可汗整合汗國之後，不斷南下窺伺河套、靈州與朔州，擾掠糧道、驅趕牧畜，與唐的邊軍在漠南反覆拉鋸，兩邊累積舊怨。內附的鐵勒契苾部與突厥本為同族世仇，契苾明等願藉唐軍之力雪舊恨、掃清漠南的舊部，使唐廷得到內應與嚮導。唐廷的算盤則是趁默啜權力尚在整合之際，以北衙禁軍的精銳出塞打一次主動的殲滅戰，恢復陰山一線的屏障，切斷突厥右部與西域的往來，並藉此向西域諸國示強，同時牽制西面吐蕃的壓力。雙方都明白，邊界的強弱在此一役中不只關乎土地，更關乎能否守住通往西域的商道與使節通道；一場勝仗帶來的降附與俘獲，往往比城池本身更能改變談判的籌碼。同樣地，突厥之所以在漠南用兵，除了掠奪芻粟，也是要壓住附唐諸部的分離傾向，雙方的進退皆繫於部族向背。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the southward pressure of the Eastern Turks. Once the Khaganate had been welded together under Muqie, its riders pressed south again and again against Hetao, Lingzhou and Shuozhou, raiding the supply lines and driving off the herds, and the border troops of the two sides ground against each other along the southern steppe until old scores had piled up. The Tiele Qiebi, long subject to the Turks and carrying a feud of their own against that house, were willing to use the Tang army to pay that debt back and to sweep the steppe clear of their old kinsmen, and so the court obtained guides and allies from within. The Tang calculation was to seize the moment while the new Khagan was still consolidating, to take the elite of the Northern Palace guards out of the frontier and strike a deliberate annihilating blow, restoring the Yinshan line as a shield, cutting the Turkic right wing off from the western regions, showing the states of the west that Tang power had not declined, and at the same time tying down the pressure of the Tibetans in the west. Both sides understood that the strength of the frontier in this campaign was not only a matter of land: it was a matter of holding the trade routes and the channels of envoys that led westward, and the surrenders and captives won by a single victory often changed the terms of negotiation more than the taking of a walled town would have done. Equally, the Turkic campaigning in the southern steppe was not only a raid for fodder; it was an attempt to hold down the separatist drift of the groups that had gone over to the Tang, and the movements of both sides turned on how the tribes would lean.
impact: 就當時而言，東硤谷一役是武周末年唐對突厥少數記錄清晰的野戰勝利。斬首千餘級、俘人畜十餘萬的數字說明唐軍並非只在邊城守禦，禁軍與邊軍配合得出的追擊戰同樣能打到草原深處；所獲牲畜大量轉為軍中芻秣，暫時補足了遠征最缺的馬匹與肉食。契苾部等內附部族藉此鞏固了在漠南的地位，與唐的關係更為深入，薛仁貴的晚節名聲亦因此更盛。此役之後，突厥勢力一度退往漠北，陰山沿線的邊防壓力稍緩；但史籍並未記載由此而出現根本性的戰局反轉，數年後突厥仍大舉南下，河套一線再成兵地，而唐廷用兵的方向，也由此次的追擊轉為以守禦與屯田為主的長期對峙。對後世讀史者而言，此役亦是觀察唐代邊防編制與草原戰法的一扇窗口。所俘牲畜與器械若能如期轉為軍資，則邊軍的續戰能力便有可觀的改善，這是遠征真正的收益所在。
impactEn: For the time, the battle of Dongxie Valley was one of the few clearly recorded field victories the Tang won over the Turks in the last years of the Wu regime. The record of more than a thousand heads taken and of over one hundred thousand people and livestock captured shows that the Tang were not merely holding town walls: a pursuit fought by the palace guards in concert with the frontier troops could reach deep into the grassland, and the captured animals were turned in large numbers into fodder and meat, easing the worst shortage of the expedition, horses and provisions. The Tiele groups under Tang allegiance, the Qiebi among them, used the victory to consolidate their standing in the southern steppe and to draw closer to the Tang, and the late reputation of Xue Rengui was enhanced by it. Afterwards the Turkic strength withdrew for a time towards the northern desert and the pressure along Yinshan eased; but no history records any fundamental reversal of the strategic situation, and a few years later the Turks came south in force again, Hetao became a theatre of war once more, and the Tang turned from the offensive pursuit of this campaign to a long contest fought from fortified positions and garrison farms. For later readers of the histories this battle is also a window onto the frontier establishment of the Tang and on the way steppe warfare was actually conducted. If the captured animals and equipment could be turned into army stores on time, the ability of the frontier troops to keep fighting would improve appreciably, and that was where the real profit of the expedition lay.
result: 唐軍在東硤谷追上東突厥騎兵並將其擊潰，記錄中最常見的結果是斬首千餘級、俘人畜十餘萬，突厥部眾潰散，退往漠北方向，默啜汗國在漠南的攻勢為之一挫。對唐而言，陰山與河套一線的邊境壓力暫時減輕，契苾部等內附部眾的地位更穩。但史載止於此役的斬獲數字，並無追擊至牙帳的記載；兩《唐書》與《資治通鑑》的相關條目都極為簡略，雙方損耗、戰役時長與具體戰場方位皆無可徵之處，學者對東硤谷的地望仍有諸說並存，或指陰山北麓，或指雲中、定襄以北。本戰役因此只能視為一次邊境層面的戰術性勝利，而不是對東突厥的決定性打擊，其真正的影響，仍須放在後續數年的邊疆起伏中一併衡量。而所謂「俘人畜十餘萬」究竟指生擒之眾，抑或連同牛羊帳具一併計算，也留待後人裁斷。
resultEn: The Tang army caught the Eastern Turkic horse at Dongxie Valley and broke them; the outcome most often recorded is that more than a thousand heads were taken and over one hundred thousand people and livestock were captured, the Turkic masses scattered and withdrew towards the northern desert, and the offensive of the Khaganate in the southern steppe received a check. For the Tang the pressure on the Yinshan and Hetao line was eased for the time, and the position of the Tiele groups under Tang allegiance, the Qiebi among them, grew more secure. Yet the record stops at the figure of the booty; there is no account of a pursuit reaching the khagan's own camp, and the relevant entries in the Old and New Tang histories and in the Comprehensive Mirror are extremely brief. Losses on both sides, the length of the fighting and the exact site of the battle cannot be verified, and scholars still differ over where Dongxie Valley lay, some placing it on the northern slopes of Yinshan, others to the north of Yunzhong and Dingxiang. This campaign can therefore be judged only a tactical success on the frontier scale, not a decisive blow against the Eastern Turks, and its true effect has to be weighed against the rises and falls of the border in the years that followed. And whether the phrase about one hundred thousand people and livestock captured refers to persons actually taken alive, or counts cattle, sheep and tentage along with them, is left for later scholars to decide.
